sections.content: How many people are "other drivers and transport operatives"?

16,585 people

were counted on the census as "other drivers and transport operatives" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may monitor the activities of bus drivers, conductors and other road transport depot drivers, undertake various tasks related to water transportation, and perform other transportation tasks not elsewhere classified.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "other drivers and transport operatives" there were more men than women (81.8% compared with 18.2%).

This means "other drivers and transport operatives" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "transport and mobile machine drivers and operatives".

Men made up 81.9% and women made up 18.1% of "other drivers and transport operatives"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "other drivers and transport operatives" included:

  • cyber security professionals
  • directors in logistics, warehousing and transport
  • farmers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "other drivers and transport operatives" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "other drivers and transport operatives", 13.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "other drivers and transport operatives" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "other drivers and transport operatives" included:

  • information technology trainers
  • careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists
  • protective service associate professionals (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "other drivers and transport operatives" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "other drivers and transport operatives" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "other drivers and transport operatives", 8.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (91.8% compared with 8.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (89.2%) than self-employed (10.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
